messages:
Alex Kim: quick sync — i pushed a short RFC: proposing a hybrid edge proxy that accepts both REST/JSON and gRPC, and translates to an internal protobuf-first service mesh. main goals: keep client ergonomics, avoid duplicate backend impls, and centralize quotas + routing policies. https://rfc.internal/edge-hybrid

Priya Shah: curious — where do quotas live in this model? at the edge proxy (single source) or in each service (fine-grained)?

Alex Kim: thinking: primary rate/usage quotas at the edge (billing/cost isolation), per-service quotas as secondary for DoS protection. edge enforces tenant-level tokens + global burst limits.

Marco Ortega: +1 for edge enforcement for billing. but if we offload enforcement to edge we need strong telemetry hooks so services can still emit per-route usage for debug/alerts.

Samir Patel: streaming gRPC is tricky for translation. websocket/streaming clients -> edge -> backend gRPC streaming needs passthrough rather than naive JSON chunking. otherwise we lose backpressure semantics.

Alex Kim: agreed. plan is: 1) passthrough for true bidi/streaming endpoints 2) translation for unary RPCs only. annotate methods in proto with option (edge_passthrough = true).

Priya Shah: how do we propagate tracing / sampling? we should carry trace id and span hints so the edge shows up in traces. also quota decisions should tag spans with quota_bucket.

Marco Ortega: add header rules: x-rd-trace, x-rd-quota-bucket, x-rd-tenant. envoy config can map those into access logs and OTel attributes.

Jen O'Neill: rollout UX note: product wants a way to test routing policies per-tenant before flipping globally. can we support header-based canary and a console toggle? e.g. a route rule: match header x-canary-variant: blue -> send to new backend.

Alex Kim: yes — router supports tag-based routing: header, cookie, and ip-prefix. console will expose a canary toggle per route plus an override list (tenants or API keys).

Samir Patel: perf concern: translation adds 1 extra proxy hop for unary calls (client -> edge -> service). we should benchmark CPU cost of JSON<->proto for 1000rps 512 token payloads. can we do accelerated path with proto over http2?

Alex Kim: acceleration plan: when client speaks gRPC we forward HTTP/2 protobuf directly (no translation). only when client sends JSON do we translate. also consider shared memory pool for translation to reduce allocations.

Priya Shah: telemetry: need per-token costs and latency breakdown (edge translate, service inference, kv-cache). will surface in console traces and per-route dashboards.

Marco Ortega: can we include an optional sampling of request/response payloads (redacted) for regression debugging? must be opt-in per-tenant and logged to secure bucket.

Jen O'Neill: also add rollback policy for model-serving endpoints: automatic fallback to smaller model variant on errors or tail-latency > threshold for X minutes. console should show active fallback and allow manual revert.

Alex Kim: noted. I'll add fallback policy hooks to the router: canary rules, automatic fallback, and metrics emissions (fallback_reason).

deploy-bot: deploy started: edge-proxy/rfc-hybrid v1 -> staging by Alex Kim (1738259050) :rocket:

Marco Ortega: small ops ask — when edge enforces token/quota, we need a reasonable TTL for token validation cache (10s?) to avoid auth backend load.

Priya Shah: 10s seems fine, but ensure revocation windows documented (expected worst-case 10s).

Samir Patel: action items: I'll prototype streaming passthrough + backpressure test harness.

Alex Kim: action items: 1) update RFC with proto annotation + header mappings 2) add console canary toggle mock 3) perf benchmarking plan.

Jen O'Neill: happy to own console mock and rollout UX flows.

Alex Kim: cool — if no objections i'll merge RFC in 24h and kick off prototyping. call out any blockers here. :thumbsup:

Priya Shah: no blockers from infra side.

Marco Ortega: one note — security review for payload sampling before merge. will start it.

Alex Kim: thanks all.
